newsitem.title: CHILE: U.S. rescue yacht is wrecked on Easter Island.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rescue yacht is wrecked on Easter Island.

text.p: An American yacht that rescued the crew of a primitive reed boat sailing across the Pacific on a trans-oceanic expedition has itself been wrecked in a storm on Chile's Easter Island, radio reports said on Friday.

The Stray Dog was battered against rocks on Thursday while moored at Easter Island, destroying its bow, but its crew managed to save $30,000 in electrical equipment aboard, radio broadcasters in Santiago said. The yacht's captain Brian Scott could not be reached for comment.

The Stray Dog went to the rescue of the reed boat Mata Rangi last week when it split in two during a storm while sailing to Tahiti. The replica of ancient Polynesian vessels was piloted by Spanish adventurer Kitin Munoz with funds from the U.N. cultural agency UNESCO and the Spanish royal family.

The American yacht rescued all 13 crew members from life rafts and brought them back to Easter Island, where they had built the ship with reeds and launched it on May 5. They had hoped to sail to New Zealand and Samoa.

The wreck of the Stray Dog is the latest bad luck to hit the Mata Rangi project. Its planned launch by Spain's Prince Felipe was delayed by bad weather until after his departure, the boat was found to have two stowaways with criminal records aboard, and a member of the Stray Dog's crew suffered food poisoning at a thank-you barbecue for the Mata Rangi rescue.
